facts.answer:
Stripe::RequestParams.coerce_value supports :int64_string for positive and negative integers including signed 64-bit limits, recurses through object and array schemas, and leaves fields without that encoding unchanged.

[Owner contract details]
Signed-int64 boundaries and composite traversal: :int64_string encodes Integer to decimal integer String and decodes it to Integer, including both signed 64-bit limits. Arrays of encoded leaves are coerced elementwise. Unsupported leaf types pass through; invalid numeric strings on decode raise ArgumentError. Object and array schemas recurse without mutating input; mismatched non-container values remain unchanged. Nullable schemas preserve nil. A discriminated union reads String or Symbol discriminator keys and values; known tags select their schema and unknown name-like tags pass through. Missing, nil or non-name-like tags raise ArgumentError during request encoding and pass through during decoding. Undeclared encodings pass through.

facts.answer:
A Stripe::StripeObject field declared with :decimal_string decodes a wire string to precision-preserving BigDecimal, while Stripe::RequestParams.coerce_value encodes BigDecimal, Integer, Float, and arrays for that schema as non-exponential decimal strings.

[Owner contract details]
Decimal encoding accepts BigDecimal, Integer and Float and applies elementwise to arrays. Decoding restores precision-preserving BigDecimal. Invalid numeric strings on decode raise ArgumentError. Output must use fixed-point spelling without an exponent; equivalent trailing zeroes are not significant. Nil and unsupported leaf types pass through. Nested response objects apply their own declared field encodings.
